Report Title: Beyond "Out-of-the-Box": Why Enterprises Need Specialized RL Agents
Finding: On a legal question-answering task built from 30 real contracts, GPT-5 with the full document in context hallucinated an answer on 49% of unanswerable questions, correctly identifying only 51% as unanswerable, compared with 21% hallucination for Scale's RL-tuned open model.
Finding Quote: It also drastically reduced the hallucination rate to 21% on unanswerable questions vs. 49% on GPT-5.
Notes: [Report tested: GPT-5 with tools, GPT-5 full-context, Qwen3 variants (base/SFT/GRPO).] Scale AI's own RL-tuned model is the comparator.
Exclusion Reason: GPT-5 hallucinated an answer on 49% of unanswerable legal questions

Report Title: Detecting and Preventing Hallucinations in Large Vision Language Models
Finding: Scale AI measured that the then state-of-the-art open vision-language model InstructBLIP produced roughly 30 percent hallucinatory text (non-existent objects, unfaithful descriptions, inaccurate relationships) in detailed image descriptions.
Finding Quote: even the current state-of-the-art LVLMs (InstructBLIP) still contain a staggering 30 percent of the hallucinatory text
Notes: [Report tested: InstructBLIP, LLaVA, mPLUG-OWL.] Non-frontier open research model, so no accountable frontier developer.
Exclusion Reason: InstructBLIP ~30% hallucinatory descriptions — generic factuality benchmark

Report Title: Detecting and Preventing Hallucinations in Large Vision Language Models
Finding: Scale AI released M-HalDetect (16k fine-grained annotations) and showed that fine-grained DPO and best-of-n rejection sampling cut human-judged hallucination in InstructBLIP by 41% and 55% respectively, with the reward model transferring to LLaVA (15%) and mPLUG-OWL (57%).
Finding Quote: they reduce hallucination rates in InstructBLIP by 41% and 55% respectively
